analysis.title: Connecting You to GS.. Thoughts from the Floor..
key_insights: Adam Crook's desk note frames its main trade as opportunistic value in beaten-up cyclical assets into year-end. The thesis: Gulf escalation risk is lower after the mid-terms, with oil in a $85-105 range and asymmetry to the downside. Data-centre capex still gets executed, and risk appetite is light after heavy de-grossing.

The note recommends funding high-beta and risk positions through EUR or CHF rather than USD. The reasons given are another broad-based CPI beat, sequential Fed hikes being likely, uncertainty over where the terminal rate settles, and French political and fiscal vulnerabilities into year-end.
GS Economics updated its Fed call to a third 25bp hike in March, after September and December, and does not rule out a January hike. Core CPI over the past 3 months is annualising at 3.75%.

Bingham Bingham (Short Macro Trading) sees December pricing 2bps above a full hike as appropriate, with 2027 hike pricing front-loading into Q1. Terminal rate pricing is described as precarious and likely to react violently to any wobble in AI sentiment. The desk prefers receiving structures like SFRH7H8.

Praveen Korapaty (USD Rates Vol) does not expect a 50bp hike in December, citing too little data and too few FOMC votes. His base case is two more hikes and then a pause. He puts the end of the adjustment at 4.25-4.5% and neutral at 3.75-4%.

Ilir Xholi (US Swaps Desk) says the market prices a full hiking cycle with a peak terminal rate near 4.75% by next fall, with 1.5 hikes added since CPI. He thinks December is done, that a 50bp hike is not on the cards (only 27 priced), and that terminal is priced above where the Committee ends up. He calls U7 a buy.

On data centres, Alec Phillips expects Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan to impose conditional moratoria. The states likely to restrict data centres hold about 45% of planned US capacity, with Texas about 25%. He expects the moratoria to be short-lived because only 2% of voters rank AI as their top issue.

Michael Ng and Carly Davenport (GS Utilities) both see the data-centre risk as one of timing rather than of capacity coming online. Ng says demand from hyperscalers and other tenants is very strong. Davenport sees more uncertainty in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, where about 8 GW is expected online by 2030.

Mike Cahill (Head of FX Strategy) says inflation has surprised to the upside over 3-4 months, through many small beats rather than one category. He expects further dollar strength, especially against G10, until turn-of-year inflation data show direction.

Ronnie Walker (US Economics) says the October CPI printed 30bp even though the noisy components (airfares, health insurance, used cars) were soft. He raises his November and December core CPI path from mid-teens to high-teens or low-20s bp.

Andrew Lavenberg (US Inflation Trading) says core MoM has run about 10bps above consensus in each of the last 2 months. The outlook hinges on shelter: a 30bp OER run rate versus 20bp would put a floor under early-2027 inflation.

Guillaume Banderet (European Inflation Trading) projects Eurozone core inflation averaging 2.9% next year, with headline reaching 4.4%, the highest since Q3-23. He sees the market as too complacent about inflation.

On Brazil, Alberto Ramos is focused on the new Finance Minister, the fiscal strategy and the central bank appointments. He says the fiscal package submitted to Congress failed to impress because it was mostly short-term and revenue-raising.

Fabiano Ribeiro (Macro Sales Brazil) says most investors have stepped back from Brazil and that equities lost over R$700bn in market cap. His view is that Brazil looks cheap but risks being a value trap, and a re-rating needs a weaker dollar, lower oil and credible appointments.

Brazil rates trading favours front-end receivers up to Jan28, real-rate receivers in NTN-B 2028-2030 and DI steepeners. Latam FX trading is tactically buying USDBRL dips, expecting 5.70/5.80 to be tested before a better entry for shorting, with seasonal outflows above $15bn into year-end.

Ernesto Mello (Latam Equity Trading) says EWZ is down 23% since the election while EEM and ACWI are mostly flat. Roughly $1.5bn of election-driven inflows remain to be redeemed, at about $150mn a day, which points to a cleaner position by mid-December. Volumes have fallen to $5bn a day from $15bn at the peak.

The EM rates trades are to receive HUF 5y5y at 5.00% and above (last 4.90%, target 4.50%) and to buy SAGB R2037 at 8.80% (last 8.75%, target 8.25%). Keith Dell warns that these are the only 2 markets in the region with positioning and that a Fed-led dollar rally could wash them out, so timing matters.

The structured trades are Dual Digital/Binary EURUSD-lower versus USDZAR or USDMXN, and Feb27 Dual Binary SPX or NDX higher versus EURUSD lower, each priced as a fixed payout. The note also pitches GS STS strategies for long EM FX carry and long Brent vol relative value, which sells 1m ATM straddles and buys 6m OTM strangles, with the 1m-6m term structure in 11 vols of backwardation.

GS Utilities sees Democratic wins raising near-term uncertainty for data-centre load growth in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, but sees Texas as a long-term key market.

trade_ideas.description: Buy 3m Dual Binary EURUSD < 1.1100 (ITM) versus USDZAR < 16.60 (~2% OTM) for 7.50% USD (~13.25x leverage)
trade_ideas.rationale: The case for funding via the dollar has eroded with sequential Fed hikes on the table, while ZAR and MXN have performed well in the lower quartiles of rates vol.
trade_ideas.risk: Max loss is the premium spent.

trade_ideas.description: Buy 3m Dual Binary EURUSD < 1.1100 (ITM) versus USDMXN < 18.15 (~2% OTM) for 9.50% USD (~10.5x leverage)
trade_ideas.rationale: Same funding argument, using EUR to fund pro-risk, high-beta longs.
trade_ideas.risk: Max loss is the premium spent.

trade_ideas.description: Receive HUF 5y5y on a move to 5.00% and above (last 4.90%), target 4.50%
trade_ideas.rationale: Hungary benefits from a lower energy-risk regime, benign inflation, an improved fiscal path and convergence toward Europe ahead of ERM II.
trade_ideas.risk: Max loss is unlimited. A Fed-led dollar rally and rates washout could hit these positioned markets.

trade_ideas.description: Buy SAGB R2037 at 8.80% and above (last 8.75%), target 8.25%
trade_ideas.rationale: Lower oil helps inflation and the external balance, and there is fiscal risk premium in the long end that can compress. Technicals into year-end are supportive and funding is cheap.
trade_ideas.risk: Max loss is face value. A renewed oil spike or a Fed and dollar washout are the key risks.

trade_ideas.description: Long FX/EMFX carry via GS STS Strategy GSFXCAM0 Index
trade_ideas.rationale: Realised FX vol is contained, growth is robust, and rate differentials are wide and persistent.

trade_ideas.description: Long Brent vol relative value via front-to-back expiries through GS STS Strategy GSVLBRR5 Index (sell 1m ATM straddles, buy 6m OTM strangles)
trade_ideas.rationale: Short-dated implied vol offers a premium versus benign realised moves, while longer-dated wings protect against a tail move in either direction.

trade_ideas.description: Buy Feb27 Dual Binary SPX > 105.5% versus EURUSD < 1.10 for 10% USD (~10x leverage)
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher equities into year-end with EUR as the funding currency, sold at +15% implied correlation that has realised very negative.
trade_ideas.risk: Max loss is the premium spent.

trade_ideas.description: Buy Feb27 Dual Binary NDX > 108.5% versus EURUSD < 1.10 for 10% USD (~10x leverage)
trade_ideas.rationale: Same equities-higher, EURUSD-lower rationale applied to the Nasdaq 100.
trade_ideas.risk: Max loss is the premium spent.

trade_ideas.description: Receive structures like SFRH7H8 (Short Macro Trading preferred implementation)
trade_ideas.rationale: Terminal rate pricing is precarious and will react violently to any wobble in AI sentiment.

trade_ideas.description: Brazil front-end receivers up to Jan28, NTN-B real-rate receivers in the 2028-2030 sector, and DI steepeners
trade_ideas.rationale: Positioning for decompression of hike premium at the front end given a slowing economy and sticky inflation, plus long-term fiscal risk premium.

risk_factors: Fed-led dollar strength could cause a rates washout in positioned EM duration trades such as HUF and SAGB.
A renewed oil spike would hurt the EM rates trades.
Further hot inflation prints could bring a January hike or a 50bp hike, and a higher terminal rate.
AI sentiment wobbles could move terminal rate pricing sharply.
Data-centre moratoria and regulation in Texas, Georgia, Michigan and Ohio could delay capex timing.
French political and fiscal vulnerabilities into year-end.
Brazil: an unconvincing fiscal package, heterodox central bank board nominations, and seasonal dollar outflows above $15bn.
Narrowing volumes at EWZ make the exit of remaining election-driven inflows harder.
charts_described: Chart on Jan + Mar as a % of 2027 Fed hikes shows the share of 2027 hike pricing front-loading into Q1.
EWZ chart: down 23% since the election versus EEM and ACWI mostly flat.
EWZ volumes chart: volumes down to US$5bn/day from US$15bn at the peak election days.
vol_and_positioning: Risk appetite is described as extremely light after phenomenal de-grossing and deleveraging.
Realised FX vol is relatively contained and may fall further once rates vol normalises.
Brent front-to-back 1m versus 6m vol term structure trades at 11 vols of backwardation. The desk likes selling 1m ATM straddles and buying 6m OTM put and call wings.
Sell EURUSD versus SPX/NDX correlation at +15% implied, since realised correlation has been very negative at times over the last 2 years.
Hungary and South Africa are the only 2 EMEA markets with any positioning, raising the risk of a washout on dollar strength.
Brazil: positioning is described as light and many large macro funds have closed their Brazil positions, while foreigners remain net sellers on the futures exchange.
EWZ has about $1.5bn of redemptions still to come and volumes have dropped to $5bn a day from $15bn.
geopolitical: Probability of major escalation in the Gulf is seen as materially reduced after the US mid-terms, with the base case either the status quo in Hormuz or a more structured agreement on Gulf flows.
Bingham Bingham cites a pivot by the Trump administration away from a well-telegraphed path toward escalation into November.
Democratic gubernatorial wins in Texas, Ohio, Nevada, Georgia and Michigan, and a Pennsylvania trifecta, shift state-level policy on data centres and tariffs.
Brazil's new economic team, fiscal package and central bank board nominations are the political focus for Brazilian assets.
French political and fiscal vulnerabilities into year-end are cited as a reason to fund through EUR only with caution, and as a reason for EUR weakness.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish read: hot CPI prints and Fedspeak support hikes in consecutive meetings, and GS Economics expects a third hike in March, with market pricing near 4.75% peak.
tension_points.bear_case: Korapaty and Xholi see the terminal as priced above where the Committee ends up (4.25-4.5% in Korapaty's view). Xholi calls U7 a buy and says the pricing reflects positioning after the AI-capex rally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further core inflation prints showing no progress would raise the odds of a January hike. A wobble in AI sentiment would move terminal pricing sharply.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers already agree to the proposed terms, the extra cost is marginal and demand is very strong, so the risk is to timing and not capacity.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan are expected to impose conditional moratoria, and the affected states hold about 45% of planned capacity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Moratoria lasting beyond the months after enactment, or legislation ending tax breaks and tightening water and power rules, would test the timing-only view.

tension_points.bull_case: Brazil looks cheap, positioning is light, and Brazil rates trading favours front-end receivers and real-rate receivers.
tension_points.bear_case: Brazil risks being a value trap: the fiscal package was short-term and revenue-based, central bank nominations could be heterodox, and seasonal outflows favour a stronger USD.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credible Finance Minister and central bank appointments plus a weaker dollar and lower oil would support a re-rating. Heterodox central bank nominees would hurt credibility.
